messages.content: is my sister need a book correct?
use my sister needs a book. needs goes with my sister in that sentence.
now make it about me.
i need a book.
why not needs after i?
with i, use need here. with she or my sister, use needs: she needs a book.
ask whether she needs one.
does she need a book?
why did needs change back to need after does?
in that question, does goes with need. she needs a book says it is true, and does she need a book asks whether it is true.
give just the correct sentence and question together.
she needs a book. does she need a book?
now answer no in a full sentence.
no, she does not need a book.
only give a question asking what she needs.
what does she need?
write a story about a child seeing a photo of the kitchen and asking why the table is in the wrong place. the photo should be from before the room changed.

a child found a photo of her family eating in the kitchen. she saw the table near the window and said the picture was wrong because their table was now by the door. her mother explained that the family had moved it before the child could remember. the photo had kept the room as it was on that day. they looked for what else had changed and found a small shelf that was no longer there. the child went into the kitchen and looked from the window to the door. the room she knew and the room in the photo were the same room at different parts of its story. she drew the kitchen as it looked now and put her drawing near the old photo.
why did the child first think the photo was wrong?
she knew the table by the door and saw it near the window in the photo.
did moving the table change the old photo?
no. the photo still showed the room as it was when the picture was taken.
what could the drawing add next to the photo?
it could show how the kitchen looked now, so they could see both the old and new places.
make that answer shorter.
the drawing could show the kitchen now.
can you know the specific time the table moved?
no. the story says it moved before the child could remember, but gives no specific day or year.
only give what we do not know about the time.
we do not know the specific day or year when the table moved.
finish with her asking about another room.
after looking at both pictures, she asked whether the bedroom had changed too. her mother went to find another photo.
i want to tell my brother i cannot visit today. do not tell him he should not feel sad.
you could say: i cannot visit today. i wanted to let you know before you made a plan around it.
can you make it more kind without choosing his feeling?
i am sorry i cannot visit today. i wanted to tell you before you made a plan around it.
what if i can come tomorrow but only if my work is done?
then keep that part open: i may come tomorrow if my work is done.
only give the new sentence.
i may come tomorrow if my work is done.
put both days into a short message.
i am sorry i cannot visit today. i may come tomorrow if my work is done, but i cannot be sure yet.
why not say i will be there tomorrow?
because you said you can come only if your work is done. that part is still open.
make that explanation shorter.
your work may not be done, so tomorrow is not sure yet.
only give the sentence about today.
i am sorry i cannot visit today.
i usually read before dinner, but today i read after. it was not a big change, but i liked it.
what did you like about reading after dinner?
i was not thinking about when to stop for food. i could stay with the page.
that change gave you a different kind of reading time today.
i do not want to say everyone should read after dinner.
you do not need to. it worked for you today, and that is enough information for your own choice.
help me write it in one sentence.
i liked reading after dinner today because i did not have to stop for food.
make that sentence shorter.
i liked reading after dinner because i did not need to stop for food.
does today make it a rule for tomorrow?
no. today keeps the sentence about this day. you can choose again tomorrow.
now just give a reply that does not ask another question.
you found a small change you enjoyed today.
my mother called my aunt. then my aunt called her sister, who is my mother. how many different people are in those calls?
two different people: your mother and your aunt.
why not three?
the person your aunt called was your mother. that was the same person already in the first call.
explain with the word she.
you said that the person your aunt called was your mother. she was already one of the two people.
now my father calls my aunt too.
then three different people have been in the calls: your mother, your aunt, and your father.
can you know they all spoke at once?
no. you gave one call, then another, then another. you did not say everyone was on the same call at once.
make that explanation shorter.
being in those calls does not mean everyone talked together at once.
now only give how many different people.
three.
can you know whether each person has their own phone?
no. being part of a call does not tell us whether someone has their own phone.
if i say this book is not as easy as that one, does that mean i cannot read it?
no. it says the two books are different in how easy they are for you. it does not say one is impossible to read.
use a sentence with both ideas.
this book is not as easy as that one, but i can still read it.
now give a short example about understanding the book.
this story has hard words, but i understand most of it.
can something take longer without being impossible?
yes. you may need more time or help and still finish it.
only give that idea without yes.
you may need more time or help and still finish it.
now make it about a drawing.
this drawing is not as easy as the other one, but i can try it slowly.
why not say i will do every part right?
because you do not know that for sure. you can try slowly without saying how every part will turn out.
make that explanation shorter.
you can try slowly without knowing for sure how it will turn out.
write a story about a person who does not know the answer to a family question and keeps it for someone who might know. do not make up the answer at the end.

a child found an old family picture and asked his father who had taken it. his father could name the people in the picture, but did not know who had held the camera. instead of choosing someone who was not in the picture, he wrote the question on the back of a page. they put it with the photo to ask the grandmother when she visited. the child asked whether leaving the answer open made the picture less useful. his father said they could still enjoy seeing the family together and learn other things from it. the question could wait while they looked at what they already knew.
what did the father know?
he knew the people in the picture, but not who had used the camera.
why not choose someone outside the picture?
not being in the picture does not tell us that the person took it. there could be another reason they were not there.
make that explanation shorter.
a person can be out of the picture without being the person who took it.
what did the note do?
it kept the question ready for a later conversation with someone who might know.
can the grandmother be sure to know?
no. she might know, but the story does not say that she does.
finish with the question still open.
they put the photo and the page together. when the grandmother came, they would ask her what she remembered.
is a cup an object? answer only yes or no.
yes.
now give a full sentence.
a cup is an object.
is every object a cup? just yes or no again.
no.
now explain that in one sentence.
a cup is an object, but a book is also an object and is not a cup.
make that explanation shorter.
a cup is an object, but a book is also an object and is not a cup.
can you say that more simply?
not all objects are cups.
only give the word for a thing that holds water.
container.
can a cup be a container too?
yes. a cup can be both an object and a container.
only give yes or no for that last question.
yes.
